title: Comparison-site core of finite dualizing restriction transport
statement: For n ≤ m ≤ r and every K at finite coefficient level n, the comparison-site and intrinsic factors of the finite dualizing restriction transport agree before appending the final normalized n ≤ m restriction component.

proof.text: Prove the ordinary comparison-restriction composition square privately. Apply the conjugation equivalence for the composite comparison and restriction/coextension adjunctions. Conjugation preserves composition, whiskering and associators. Each comparison-restriction conjugate is the identity by definition; after extensionality the remaining coextension composition square is reflexive on sections. This is the ordinaryRestrictionComp argument already proved privately in Sheaf.Paper.NormalizedOriginComparisonCoherence, reproduced locally without changing that module or its visibility.

proof.text: Apply the proved source-library theorem Functor.mapDerivedCategorySquareIso_hom_app_comp to the ordinary square and the ordinary scalar-restriction compositors. The resulting derived triangle is definitionally Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalarsCompIso, and the derived squares are pbcDerivedComparisonRestrict. Cancel the direct comparison hom and the two successive comparison homs to obtain the inverse composition equation.

proof.text: Specialize to the three finite dualizing quotient maps using finiteDualizingQuotient_comp. Map the inverse composition equation through the intrinsic equivalence at level r, append the inverse intrinsic restriction comparison for m ≤ r, and apply its naturality to the inverse n ≤ m comparison-site restriction map. Functoriality and associativity give exactly the asserted equality. Only naturality is needed: the separate intrinsic restriction composition theorem is not used.
